note: Curated, illustrative fault scenarios for the mission run. Values are team-chosen teaching cases, not NASA failure statistics or real anomaly reconstructions.

scenarios.summary: No injected fault; the outcome follows from the site, date and vehicle alone.
Descent engine limited to 80 % of maximum thrust from 200 s after powered descent initiation.
Slow propellant leak of 0.5 kg/s for 10 minutes; the landing margin shrinks.
Propellant leak of 1.5 kg/s from 60 s after powered descent initiation.
Specific impulse drops to 90 % of nominal from 100 s after powered descent initiation.
Navigation estimate drifts 600 m east; the lander touches down away from the surveyed point.
Landing waved off and retried 24 hours later; lighting and Earth geometry change.
Half of the battery capacity is lost at touchdown.
A survival heater sticks on, adding 250 W from 6 hours after landing for 48 hours.
Landing plume dust leaves the solar array at 40 % output.
The transmitter fails for 80 hours from 2 hours after landing.
A small leak during descent, then dusty panels and a stuck heater on the surface.
